title: A Film Review
description: Practise -ed/-ing adjectives and linking words, then write a review of a film you have seen.
instructions: Do the exercises in Part 1. Then write your text in Part 2.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: The ending was so ___ that I nearly fell asleep.
exercises.explanation: Use the -ing adjective to describe the thing that causes the feeling (a boring ending) and -ed for how a person feels (I was bored).

exercises.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.text: It is the funniest film I have ever ___ (see).
answers: seen
exercises.explanation: After a superlative, use the present perfect with "ever": the funniest film I have ever seen. "See" is irregular: seen.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: The film is about a girl who finds a dragon.
exercises.explanation: Put the relative clause with "who" directly after the person it describes: a girl who finds a dragon.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: I was very exciting when the film started.
answers: I was very excited when the film started.
exercises.explanation: To describe how a person feels, use the -ed adjective: I was excited.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: The special effects are amazing. ___, the story is quite weak.
exercises.explanation: "However" starts a new sentence that contrasts with the one before. "Although" must join two clauses in the same sentence.

exercises.prompt: Write the correct passive form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.text: The film ___ (direct) by a young Korean director.
answers: was directed
is directed
exercises.explanation: The passive is be + past participle. We use it when the film is more important than the person: The film was directed by ...

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: If I were you, I will watch it at the cinema.
answers: If I were you, I would watch it at the cinema.
If I were you, I'd watch it at the cinema.
exercises.explanation: The second conditional uses would, not will, in the main clause: If I were you, I would ...

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word ALTHOUGH. Begin: "Although ..."
exercises.text: The film is long, but it is never boring.
answers: Although the film is long, it is never boring.
Although it is long, the film is never boring.
Although the film is long, it is not boring.
Although the film is long, it's never boring.
Although it's long, the film is never boring.
Although the film is long, it isn't boring.
Although the film is long, it's not boring.
exercises.explanation: "Although" replaces "but" and goes at the start of the clause with the contrasting idea.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: I decided ___ the film again with my sister.
exercises.explanation: Some verbs, such as decide, want and hope, are followed by the to-infinitive: decided to watch.

exercises.prompt: Write the correct form of the word in brackets.
exercises.text: The film was a big ___ (succeed) all over the world.
answers: success
exercises.explanation: After "a big" we need a noun. The noun from "succeed" is "success".

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: I haven't seen the sequel yet.
exercises.explanation: "Yet" is used in negative sentences and questions in the present perfect, and it usually goes at the end.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: I'm not very keen on watch horror films.
answers: I'm not very keen on watching horror films.
exercises.explanation: After a preposition such as "on", use the -ing form: keen on watching.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: The book was good, but the film was even ___.
exercises.explanation: "Good" has an irregular comparative: better. "Even" makes a comparative stronger: even better.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word NEVER. Begin: "I have ..."
exercises.text: This is the first time I have seen a Korean film.
answers: I have never seen a Korean film before.
I have never seen a Korean film.
exercises.explanation: "This is the first time I have done something" means "I have never done it before".

exercises.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.text: The film ___ (come) out last month and it's already very popular.
answers: came
exercises.explanation: "Come out" means to be shown or sold to the public for the first time. With "last month" use the past simple: came.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: The film, ___ lasts three hours, is based on a true story.
exercises.explanation: Use "which" for things. Between commas (extra information) we cannot use "that".

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: You shouldn't miss this film.
exercises.explanation: Use should/shouldn't + infinitive without "to" to give advice or a recommendation.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: When I was a child, I use to watch cartoons every morning.
answers: When I was a child, I used to watch cartoons every morning.
exercises.explanation: In positive sentences the form is "used to" (with -d) + infinitive.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word OLD. Begin: "I wasn't ..."
exercises.text: I was too young to see the film at the cinema.
answers: I wasn't old enough to see the film at the cinema.
exercises.explanation: "Too + adjective" can be changed to "not + opposite adjective + enough": too young = not old enough.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word AS. Begin: "The second film ..."
exercises.text: The first film was funnier than the second one.
answers: The second film was not as funny as the first one.
The second film was not as funny as the first.
The second film was not as funny as the first film.
The second film was not as funny as the first one was.
exercises.explanation: "A was funnier than B" means "B was not as funny as A". Use the normal adjective in "as ... as".

task.prompt: An English-language website for students wants film reviews. Write a review of a film you have seen recently.
contentPoints: Name the film and say what type of film it is.
Briefly describe the story without giving away the ending.
Say what you liked and did not like.
Say who you would recommend it to.
usefulLanguage: I'd recommend it to anyone who ...
task.modelAnswer:
The Last Lighthouse is an adventure film directed by Maria Lopez. I saw it at the cinema last weekend, and it's one of the best films I've seen this year.

It tells the story of Tom, a fourteen-year-old boy who goes to stay with his grandfather on a tiny island. One stormy night, the light in the old lighthouse goes out, and Tom has to find a way to save a ship that is in danger.

What I liked most was the photography. The sea and the storms look amazing on a big screen. In addition, the young actor who plays Tom is excellent. The only problem is that the middle of the film is a bit slow.

However, I'd recommend it to anyone who loves exciting stories about the sea. If I were you, I would watch it at the cinema.
